Convert temperatures to and from 10^6/T^2

Source: R/units.R
temp2x.Rd

temp2x() converts temperatures in degrees C or kelvin to 10^6/T^2 (T in K), the scale used by all calibrations in bayclumpr. x2temp() converts them back.

Usage

temp2x(temp, tempError = NULL, unit = c("C", "K"))

x2temp(x, xError = NULL, unit = c("C", "K"))

Arguments

temp

Temperatures in degrees C or kelvin.

tempError

Optional 1 SD of temp, in the same units.

unit

Unit of temp, or the unit returned by x2temp(): "C" or "K".

x

Temperatures as 10^6/T^2 (T in K).

xError

Optional 1 SD of x.

Value

temp2x() returns a data.frame with Temperature and, when tempError is given, TempError. These names match the columns needed by the calibration functions. x2temp() returns a data.frame with Temp and, when xError is given, TempSD.

Details

Errors are propagated to first order. The SD of 10^6/T^2 is 2 x 10^6 x SD(T) / T^3, with T in kelvin. This approximation works well when the error is small relative to T, which is the case for calibration data.

Examples

temp2x(c(5, 25, 50), tempError = c(0.5, 0.5, 1))
#>   Temperature  TempError
#> 1   12.925337 0.04646894
#> 2   11.249426 0.03773076
#> 3    9.576166 0.05926762
x2temp(c(12.9, 11.3, 9.6), xError = 0.02)
#>        Temp    TempSD
#> 1  5.273023 0.2158318
#> 2 24.332059 0.2632585
#> 3 49.598612 0.3361965
